subject: [dlm vs INLA] Integrated Random Walk aka second-order random walk aka second order polynomial model with zero mean level evolution variance

messages.author: f31345e547589d21
messages.subject: [dlm vs INLA] Integrated Random Walk aka second-order random walk aka second order polynomial model with zero mean level evolution variance
parts:
Hi there,
In the attached code I simulate data according to an integrated random walk model (IRW, i.e. second order polynomial model with zero mean level evolution variance), then I process these data with the same model using the dlm package on the one hand and INLA on the other. I don't get the same results.

If the result obtained with dlm is correct, the slope variance estimated by INLA is too high. The true value is 1.073492e-16, dlm estimates it at 3.665554e-10 and inla has 1.437007e-05. Since there is an equivalence between an IRW and a second order random walk (RW2, see Hans-Peter Piepho & Joseph Ochieng Ogutu (2007) Simple State-space Models in a Mixed Model Framework, The American Statistician, 61:3, 224-232, DOI: 10.1198/000313007X220426, p 226, top of second column), I also processed the data with an RW2 in INLA, for which the estimate is 7.453803e-06.

Perhaps my writing of a second order polynomial model with zero mean level evolution variance in INLA is wrong? I've just removed the error term from the formula. Perhaps I should conclude that since the variance in the simulation is close to zero, the INLA estimate is still acceptable? However, looking at the graphs, it's clear that we won't come to the same conclusions in terms of trend and variability.

I've looked at the problem from every angle, but I can't understand this difference between dlm and INLA.

Thanks in advance for your help.
DS

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] [dlm vs INLA] Integrated Random Walk aka second-order random walk aka second order polynomial model with zero mean level evolution variance
parts:
hi

this a joint gaussian case, so there are no approximations with
essentially excact calculations, so differences should be due to
differences in the model and/or the priors.

You can start with fixing the observational variance

# Observation variance
V <- 0.2721225


like with RW2 model, its

control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1/V), fixed
= TRUE))),


I am also concerned about the

> W
[,1] [,2]
[1,] 0 0.000000e+00
[2,] 0 1.073492e-16
>


which is very very very small, so small that priors for the precision
(which you, btw, use the default ones) are nooooooo good for such
extreme values

if I use


formula.second.poly = y ~ 0 + f(i, model = "rw2", constr = FALSE,
hyper = list(prec =
list(prior = "pc.prec",
param = c(1E-8,
0.5))))


then (with fixed V),

Precision for i 1.007672257e+15 169200598521 1.007336361e+15
1.007743112e+15
0.975quant mode
Precision for i 1.008047575e+15 1.0076713e+15
[1] 9.92386158e-16
